The 1553/3708 split gives roughly 42% primary versus 58% scattered, which seems plausible. The pair fraction of 11/3708 (0.3%) also checks out against my earlier pair-to-Compton ratio assumption at 2 MeV, and 11/1553 among primaries (0.7%) matches too, so I'm now checking whether the Compton primary-to-scatter ratio holds up similarly.

Now I need to draw 200 events uniformly at random without replacement from the complete pool of 3708 recorded interactions, using a seed for reproducibility. I also want to verify the scatter fraction of 58% is reasonable physically given the scoring depth of 10 cm and field size, which seems acceptable since scattered photons shift toward lower energies with higher interaction coefficients.

For the output, I'll build JSON records per event with appropriate null fields depending on interaction type — e_out and cos_scatter null for photoelectric/pair events, cos_electron null for Rayleigh, t_e set to 0.0 for Rayleigh, and t_positron only populated for pair production — then proceed to sample the 200 events.
